chunks: From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wassash, from Rifah ibn Musa, who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: The partner (mudarib) says to the owner (sahib): If you cause him harm or consume his capital, you are liable (guarantor) for him; and he (the mudarib) is liable if he violates the condition.

key_terms.الْمُضَارِبُ: The partner who manages the business or labor
key_terms.شَرْطُهُ: The agreed condition or term of the partnership
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْمَالِ: The owner of the capital (implied by sahib)

ai.seo_question: What is the liability distribution between the capital provider and the manager in an Islamic mudarabah partnership?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the risk-allocation mechanism in mudarabah, emphasizing that the capital provider bears the financial loss unless the manager is negligent or breaches specific contractual terms. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that liability is tied to fault (*taqsir*) or deviation from the agreed conditions, distinguishing it from simple equity sharing. This hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the fiduciary duties inherent in Islamic partnership contracts.
